transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... people keep acting like I'm just imagining things. But I know what's going on. The hospital people, and some of the folks from the cleaning agency I work for, they've been watching our house. They even keep an eye on my cleaning routes when I'm at work. They're doing it to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. I just want people to stop telling me it's not happening when I know for a fact that it is.
Can you tell me more about how you know these people are watching you? Have you noticed any specific behaviors or signs that make you certain this is happening?

Well, it's just obvious if you pay attention. Like... when I'm out on my cleaning routes, I'll see the same cars parked down the street from the houses I'm working at. And then, when I get home, I'll see people walking past our house, just kind of lingering, looking at the windows. Sometimes it's people I recognize from the hospital where my husband had his appointments, or folks from the agency I work for. They try to act casual, but I know what they're doing. They're checking up on me, making sure I'm doing things right with him. It's just... I just wish people would believe me instead of telling me it's all in my head.
Have there ever been times when you experienced these kinds of thoughts or feelings without also feeling depressed or manic?

Yes, actually. Um... there was a quieter spell a little while back that lasted for several weeks. I wasn't rushing around as much as I sometimes do, and I wasn't feeling down or anything—I was just sleeping a bit more, getting my rest. But even during that quiet time, I still firmly believed the agency was watching us. And I still heard the voice over by the kitchen window. So, yes, it doesn't just happen when I'm feeling all wound up or low. It's just what's happening.
Have you ever been shown or told evidence that contradicts your belief that these people are watching you, and if so, how did you react to that information?

Well, my husband tries to tell me that. He says, "Look, there's no one out there," or he'll point out that the cars I see are just neighbors' cars. And my supervisor at the cleaning agency, when I finally asked her about it, she looked at me like I was crazy and said they don't have the time or staff to follow maids around. 

But... I mean, like I said when I first came in, people just keep acting like I'm imagining it. I know what I see. I know the hospital people and the folks from the agency are watching our house and keeping an eye on my cleaning routes. They want to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. No matter what they say or what "evidence" they try to show me, it doesn't change what's actually happening. I just know it's true.
Can you tell me how you feel when people dismiss your belief that you're being watched, and have you ever doubted it yourself, even for a moment?

I don't doubt it, no. I know what I see. But when people dismiss it... well, it really gets to me. 

There are these stretches when I feel bright and strong, like I have the energy to just handle absolutely everything at home and on my routes. But if my husband or a client questions me about things, or tells me I'm wrong, I snap at them much harder than I mean to. I just lose my temper when they don't believe me.
Can you think of any time when you were able to question or doubt your belief that people were watching you, even a little bit?

No, not really. I mean... like I said a few minutes ago, I'm really only here because people keep acting like I'm just imagining the whole thing. But I don't doubt it, because I know what I see. I know the hospital people and the folks from the cleaning agency are watching our house, and I know they check on my cleaning routes. They're doing it to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. So... no, I haven't ever really questioned it, because I know it's happening.
Have you ever experienced any other unusual beliefs or delusions that weren't related to being watched, especially when you weren't feeling particularly high or low emotionally?

Well, I haven't really had any other beliefs besides them watching me. It's always been about the hospital people and the agency. But... well, you asked about when I wasn't feeling high or low. There was a quieter spell, maybe a few months ago. It lasted for several weeks where I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't rushing around with all that extra energy I mentioned before. I was just kind of steady, I guess. 

But even then, I still believed the agency was watching us. And... I still heard the voice by the kitchen window, telling me they were out there. So, it didn't really go away, even when my mood was just normal.

During times when your mood has been stable and you weren’t feeling particularly high or low, have you ever experienced any other unusual beliefs or delusions besides the belief that you're being watched?

Well, like I said, the main thing is always about them watching me. But... I guess there was something else, now that I think about it. 

During one of those times when I wasn't feeling particularly low, but I wasn't exactly... steady either... I started feeling like I was the only one who really understood what was going on. I just had this strong feeling that I was the only person with the sense and the strength to keep my husband, my home, and even some of the folks at our church safe from what was coming. It just felt like everything depended on me because nobody else was capable of handling it. But I don't know if you'd call that a belief or just... knowing my responsibilities.

During times when your mood was stable, did you ever believe that certain events, comments, or actions of others were specifically directed at you or had special meaning for you, even if they seemed unrelated to others?

No, I don't think so. I mean... unless it has to do with the agency checking up on me, I don't really look for special meanings in things. Like, if someone makes a comment at the store or something happens on the news, it's just regular stuff. It doesn't feel like it's secretly directed at me or anything like that. So, no, I haven't experienced that.

Have you ever gone a full month without hearing the voice by the kitchen window or having any other unusual experiences, like seeing things that weren't there or feeling like your thoughts were being controlled?

No, I haven't had a break like that. The voices, and that feeling that people are watching us... it's been happening for about 11 months now. So, no, it hasn't ever stopped for a whole month since it all started.
Can you describe how certain you feel about your belief that people are watching you? Is it something you consider an absolute truth, or more of a suspicion that comes and goes?

It's an absolute truth. Honestly, I'm mostly here because people keep acting like I'm just imagining it. But I know what I see. I know for a fact that the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house. They even watch my cleaning routes when I'm out at work... just to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. So it's not just a suspicion that comes and goes. I am completely certain they are doing it.
Can you tell me if your belief that people are watching you has ever changed in any way, or has it always been exactly the same in how you understand it?

It hasn't changed at all. Like I just said, the main reason I'm even here is because people keep acting like I'm imagining it. But it's always been the exact same thing... I know the hospital people and those folks from the agency have been watching our house, and they watch my cleaning routes to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. That's just what's happening, and my understanding of it hasn't shifted into anything else.
